newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening steady to higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks look set to open steady to higher on Monday, with markets keeping an eye on economic data, especially the National Association of Purchasing Managers' (NAPM) survey.
Analysts said their forecasts were prompted in part by unchanged bond prices, a stronger dollar and a rising Standard & Poors futures index.
"I see a steady to slightly higher opening, and then all eyes will be on the NAPM," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The NAPM January survey is due out at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, with a consensus estimate by economists of 53 percent against 53.8 percent for December.
"I suspect that if we see data that indicates that the strength of the fourth quarter is not going to be met in this quarter ... we will see the market rise," Cardillo said.
Markets also will be watching out for Tuesday's and Wednesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, where the course of interest rates will be decided.
However, recent swings in the Dow Jones Industrial Average and Friday's 10-point decline in the Dow suggest that markets could fall back later in the day, analysts said.

"If you look at the futures contract, they are higher and so the Dow will be higher," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "But as to the rest of the market, every day is an adventure."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average fell 244.06 points, or 1.33 percent, to close at 18,085.95.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down 15.3 at 4260.5.
The dollar was steady in Tokyo at 121.40 and was holding in Europe at 1.65 marks.
U.S. Treasuries were lower, with the long bond off 4/32 to yield 6.80 percent. The Standard & Poors futures index was up 1.50 to 789.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street said that Seagram Co Ltd has succeeded in turning around the MCA entertainment company and reviving its theme parks.
